indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: Demonstrate an understanding of quantities and place value for multi-digit numerals up to 1,000,000,000 or 1 billion
indicator.objective: Compare and order whole numbers up to 100,000 and represent the comparison using '>', '<', or =

skills.description: Choose the correct symbol (<, >, =) between two numbers up to 100,000.
Arrange a set of numbers in ascending or descending order.
Explain why one number is greater/less using place value.

misconceptions: Believing a number with more digits is always smaller
Reading '>' as 'less than' because the wide end looks bigger

questions.explanation: 45,000 has 4 ten-thousands while 54,000 has 5 ten-thousands, so 45,000 < 54,000.
questions.misconception: Choosing '>' because 45 is written before 54.

hints: The digits are exactly the same.
Equal numbers use the equals sign.
questions.explanation: Both numbers have the same digits, so 78,000 = 78,000.
questions.misconception: Choosing '<' because the numbers look long.

hints: Count the digits: 5 digits vs 6 digits.
questions.explanation: 99,999 has 5 digits and 100,000 has 6 digits, so 99,999 < 100,000.
questions.misconception: Choosing '>' because 9 is larger than 1.

questions.explanation: 30,400 has 4 hundreds while 30,040 has 0 hundreds, so 30,400 > 30,040.
questions.misconception: Choosing '<' because 040 has more digits after the comma.

questions.explanation: 60,500 has 0 thousands while 65,000 has 5 thousands, so 60,500 < 65,000.
questions.misconception: Choosing '>' because 500 looks bigger than 000.
Adding wrongly to get 35,000 and choosing '='.

questions.explanation: Both sides equal 50,000, so the correct symbol is '='.
questions.misconception: Choosing '<' because 45,000 looks smaller than 55,000.

questions.stem: Which symbol correctly completes 3 ten-thousands + 12 thousands __ 4 ten-thousands + 2 thousands?
questions.explanation: Both sides equal 42,000, so the correct symbol is '='.
questions.misconception: Choosing '<' because 3 < 4 without regrouping.

questions.explanation: Ascending means smallest to largest: 20,300; 23,000; 30,200; 32,000.
questions.misconception: Ordering by the last two digits only.
Ordering by the hundreds digit only.

hints: Look at the thousands digit first.
For numbers starting with 8, compare the hundreds digit.
questions.explanation: 8,090 has 0 hundreds, so it is the smallest.
questions.misconception: Choosing 8,900 because it looks like the smallest three-digit number 900.

hints: 60,700 is the only number starting with 60.
questions.misconception: Placing 70,600 before 67,000 because 70 > 67.
Ordering by the last digit only.
Comparing only the tens digit.

questions.explanation: 43,000 is the largest because it has the highest ten-thousands digit (4) and highest thousands digit (3) among those starting with 4.
questions.misconception: Choosing 40,300 because it has a 3 in the hundreds.

options: 100,000 has six digits while 99,999 has five digits
hints: Count the digits in each number.
A six-digit number is always greater than a five-digit number.
questions.explanation: 100,000 has 6 digits and 99,999 has 5 digits, so 100,000 is greater.
questions.misconception: Thinking 99,999 is greater because it has more 9s.

questions.stem: A pupil says 7,800 > 7,080 because 8 is bigger than 0. Explain the error.

criteria.description: States that the comparison must start from the highest place value
Explains that both numbers have 7 thousands, so the hundreds digit must be compared

hints: Both have 7 thousands; what comes next?
questions.explanation: Both numbers have 7 thousands. In the hundreds place, 7,800 has 8 and 7,080 has 0. Since 8 > 0, 7,800 is greater — but the reason is the hundreds digit, not just any 8.
questions.misconception: Looking at any digit rather than working from the highest place value.

questions.stem: Without calculating, explain why 45,000 + 8,000 is greater than 45,000 + 3,000.

criteria.description: Notes that both expressions start with 45,000
Explains that 8,000 > 3,000, so the total is greater

questions.explanation: Both expressions start with the same number, 45,000. Since 8,000 > 3,000, adding 8,000 gives a greater total.
questions.misconception: Adding both sides fully instead of comparing the addends.

questions.stem: Use place value to explain why 62,000 > 61,999.

criteria.description: Compares the thousands digit (2 > 1) and concludes 62,000 is greater

questions.explanation: Both numbers have 6 ten-thousands. In the thousands place, 62,000 has 2 while 61,999 has 1. Since 2 > 1, 62,000 > 61,999.
questions.misconception: Thinking 61,999 is greater because it has more 9s.

questions.explanation: Both have 5 thousands. In the hundreds place, 4 > 2, so 5,432 > 5,234.
questions.misconception: Comparing the entire last three digits as one number without place value.
